quote: Against this stand worries about safety and consent. Editing tools can cut at unintended sites; embryos can develop as mosaics of edited and unedited cells; and genes rarely do just one thing. The variant that causes sickle cell disease also protects against malaria, and edits made in China in 2018 to confer HIV resistance may carry cognitive effects no one tested for. Because heritable changes pass to descendants, mistakes could propagate irreversibly, and the people most affected, future generations, cannot consent.
